privacy.agent_signup.intro: Agent PRO is responsible for the data about you and your account. This notice lists what we keep, why, and for how long.
privacy.agent_signup.lapsed: If your plan lapses, your account and its data are deleted 12 months later. We remind you 30 days, 7 days and 48 hours before; renewing before then cancels the deletion.
privacy.agent_signup.no_ads: No ads, no trackers, and we never sell your data.

Supabase and Cloudflare staff may access data from outside India for support.

seed.faq.choose.answer_1: Start with what you want to protect and what losing it would cost you. Then we compare a few suitable policies on cover, exclusions and premium, and pick the one that fits your budget.
seed.faq.choose.answer_2: There's no single right answer. I'll ask about your needs, what you already have and your budget, explain what each option covers and doesn't cover, and help you decide without any pressure.
seed.faq.choose.answer_3: Tell me a little about yourself and what you'd like to protect. I'll suggest a few options, explain them in plain words and leave the decision to you.
seed.faq.choose.question: How do I choose the right cover?
seed.faq.claims.answer_1: Yes. If you or your family ever need to make a claim, I'll guide you through the forms and documents and stay in touch with the insurer at every step.
seed.faq.claims.answer_2: Of course. A claim is when you need support the most. I'll explain what's needed, help you fill in the forms, gather the documents with you and follow up until you have an answer.
seed.faq.claims.answer_3: Absolutely. Helping with claims is part of my service. Just call me, and together we'll prepare the paperwork and keep track of it until the claim is decided.
seed.faq.claims.question: Will you help with claims?
seed.faq.cover.answer_1: A common starting point is about 10 to 15 times your yearly income, plus any loans you have. The right amount depends on your family, your goals and your budget, so let's work it out together in a short chat.
seed.faq.cover.answer_2: It depends on your income, your loans and the goals you want to protect, such as your children's education. Many families start with around 10 to 15 times their annual income. Tell me a little about yours and we'll find a sensible amount together.
seed.faq.cover.answer_3: There's no single number. I look at what your family would need to keep going, such as daily expenses, loans and children's studies, and at what you already have. Then we choose cover that fits your budget.
seed.faq.cover.question: How much life cover do I need?
seed.faq.documents.answer_1: Usually a photo ID and address proof (such as Aadhaar, PAN, passport or voter ID), a recent photograph, income proof for higher cover, and your bank details. Some plans also need a medical check-up. I'll give you the exact list for the plan you choose.
seed.faq.documents.answer_2: For most plans you need KYC documents (identity and address proof, such as Aadhaar and PAN), a photograph and bank details. For larger cover, income proof and a medical test may be needed. Don't worry, I'll help you get everything ready.
seed.faq.documents.answer_3: The basics are simple: identity proof, address proof, a photo and bank details. Depending on the plan and the cover amount, income proof or a health check-up may also be asked for. I'll tell you exactly what's needed before we start.
seed.faq.documents.question: Which documents do I need to buy a policy?
seed.faq.documents_general.answer_1: Usually identity and address proof (such as Aadhaar or PAN), a photograph and details of what you want to insure. Some policies need more, such as a health check-up. I'll give you the exact list for the policy you choose.
seed.faq.documents_general.answer_2: Most policies need KYC documents (identity and address proof), a photograph and the details of what is being insured. Depending on the policy, more may be asked for. Don't worry, I'll help you get everything ready.
seed.faq.documents_general.answer_3: The basics are simple: identity proof, address proof and a photo. Each kind of policy asks for its own details, and I'll tell you exactly what's needed before we start.
seed.faq.existing.answer_1: Yes. Bring your policy documents and I'll explain what they cover, point out any gaps and keep track of their renewal dates for you.
seed.faq.existing.answer_2: Of course. A quick review often shows whether your cover is still enough. I'll go through your policies with you and explain them in plain words.
seed.faq.existing.answer_3: Sure. Share the details of your current policies and I'll help you understand them and see whether anything needs to change.
seed.faq.existing.question: Can you look at the policies I already have?
seed.faq.premium.answer_1: Most plans let you pay yearly, half-yearly, quarterly or monthly, online, by auto-debit or at a branch. I'll remind you before every due date. Premiums may also qualify for tax benefits as per prevailing tax laws.
seed.faq.premium.answer_2: You can choose a payment mode that suits your cash flow: yearly, half-yearly, quarterly or monthly. Paying online or by auto-debit is the easiest way, and I'll send you a reminder before each due date. Tax benefits may apply as per prevailing tax laws.
seed.faq.premium.answer_3: Yearly, half-yearly, quarterly or monthly: pick what fits your budget. You can pay online, set up auto-debit or pay at a branch. I keep track of your due dates and remind you in time. Any tax benefit applies as per prevailing tax laws.
seed.faq.premium.question: How can I pay my premium?
seed.faq.premium_general.answer_1: It depends on the policy: many are paid once for the whole cover period, others yearly or in instalments. You can usually pay online or by auto-debit, and I'll remind you before every renewal or due date.
seed.faq.premium_general.answer_2: Choose what suits you among the options your policy offers: a single payment for the cover period, yearly, or instalments. Paying online is the easiest way, and you'll hear from me before each due date.
seed.faq.premium_general.answer_3: Each policy has its own payment options, and I'll explain them before you buy. I also keep track of your renewal and due dates and remind you in time, so your cover never lapses by accident.
seed.faq.term_vs_savings.answer_1: Term insurance pays only if something happens to you during the policy term, so a large cover costs a low premium. A savings plan combines protection with saving and pays a benefit at maturity as per its terms, but costs more for the same cover. I'll explain both and help you choose.
seed.faq.term_vs_savings.answer_2: Think of term insurance as pure protection: the highest cover for the lowest premium, with no payout if you outlive the term. Savings plans add a maturity benefit, which means a higher premium. Many families combine the two. Let's see what suits you.
seed.faq.term_vs_savings.answer_3: Term plans focus on protecting your family at a low cost. Savings plans help you build money for goals like a child's education, along with some cover, as per the plan's terms. The right mix depends on your needs, and I'll walk you through it.
seed.faq.term_vs_savings.question: What is the difference between term insurance and a savings plan?
